issue.title: Intercepting Routes not working for multiple routes

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue was opened via the bug report template.

issue.body:
### Verify canary release

- [X] I verified that the issue exists in the latest Next.js canary release

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
      Platform: darwin
      Arch: arm64
      Version: Darwin Kernel Version 22.1.0: Sun Oct  9 20:15:09 PDT 2022; root:xnu-8792.41.9~2/RELEASE_ARM64_T6000
    Binaries:
      Node: 16.17.0
      npm: 8.15.0
      Yarn: 1.22.19
      pnpm: 7.25.1
    Relevant packages:
      next: 13.3.1-canary.3
      eslint-config-next: N/A
      react: 18.2.0
      react-dom: 18.2.0
```


### Which area(s) of Next.js are affected? (leave empty if unsure)

Intercepting Routes, Parallel Routes

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/borispoehland/nextgram-demo.git

### To Reproduce

- Open https://nextgram-demo.vercel.app/test
- Click a picture and see it **not** opening in the modal, but as page

### Describe the Bug

Route interception only works for single routes at a time. In the demo, this is https://nextgram-demo.vercel.app, but not https://nextgram-demo.vercel.app/test.

I think a very common use case will be to use the interception for each route but the intercepted route itself. For example, on all pages but `/cart,` I want the cart to render as a modal. Only when opening `https://domain.com/cart`directly, I want to render it as page. This is all the more common when you consider that a cart is often part of the nav bar, which is shown on all pages.

This behaviour currently requires to **duplicate** the intercepted segment `(..)photos/[id]/page.js` across all our routes where we want the interception to happen.

### Expected Behavior

Instead, when we declare an intercepting route as parallel route (as in the example: `@modal/(..)photos/[id]/page.js`), every layout that includes the `@modal` slot and all its children should render the modal. 

In our example, when opening the photo from within the `/test` page, it should render it as modal and not call the page, because the parent layout of the `/test` page includes the `@modal` slot
